claims.reason: The grade letter C is an editorial judgement and was not checked. The words after it describe the source: the GDPR is a legislative regulation and Art. 9 concerns special categories of data.

Searched both full-text snapshots for any comparison of the effectiveness of login or authentication methods (skuteczn-, logowan-, zalogowa-, uwierzytelni-, hasło). The GDPR text contains none. The UODO slides only report an EDPS paper's accuracy factors for biometric systems (line 317-319) and that a stolen password can be changed while fingerprints cannot (line 314-315); neither is a comparison of the effectiveness of login methods.

claims.reason: The quotes support the part that the possibility to refuse depends on the legal basis and the context: consent counts as voluntary only where refusal has no adverse consequences, and the right to object is tied to particular legal bases. No snapshot states that a person may request an alternative method; the UODO slides list 'can the person be given a choice' only as a question the controller must assess. That part is not backed.

claims.claim: Ta porada dotyczy organizacji przetwarzającej biometrię, nie jest oceną lokalnego odblokowania urządzenia.
Tekst opisuje przepisy ogólnie, nie jest poradą prawną i nie miał przeglądu prawnika.

scope_gaps.note: The sentence names only the technical-processing and identification elements; Art. 4 pkt 14 also requires that the data concern physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics. The sentence does not say these are the only elements.

A reader might assume all evidence is a legal norm; the second cited snapshot is a UODO training presentation (webinar slides of 28 April 2021 about biometrics in schools), an authority's explanation and not a norm. The sentence does not claim otherwise.

The sentence speaks of a possibility to request an alternative; the snapshots show only that a controller must assess less invasive alternatives and whether to offer a choice, not that the person can demand an alternative.
